speechtext:
Madam Speaker, on behalf of our Party I want to indicate to the Hon. Member that we would be happy to deal with this Bill immediately. In saying so, I find it remarkable that no summaries or annual returns were filed from the year 1963 to the present. It is quite astonishing that that period of time could go by without anyone being aware that no returns were filed, including 20 years elapsed from the time the company was dissolved pursuant to a notice that appeared in The Canada Gazette on June 14, 1967.
I understand that the company paid property tax and income tax throughout that period and that no person or corporation would be adversely affected by the passage of this Bill. I see the Hon. Member nodding in the affirmative.
I also note that this Bill has been passed in the Senate, but was referred to the Legal and Constitutional Affairs Committee of the other place. The solicitor on behalf of the company appeared before the Senate, as well as an official of the Department of Consumer and Corporate Affairs, who assured members of the other place that indeed this is a pro forma matter and that no person will be affected adversely by the passage of this Bill. Therefore, on that basis, we would be pleased to proceed with the passage of this Bill.

September 18, 1987
Yellowknife Electric Ltd.

subtopic: PRIVATE MEMBERS' BUSINESS-PRIVATE BILLS   YELLOWKNIFE ELECTRIC LTD.
speechtext:
Madam Speaker, on behalf of my Party, we support the motion to refer this Bill to committee. I certainly appreciate the Elon. Member's point about it being largely an administrative matter, and we do not intend to be obstructionist, but there are several points that 1 believe are worthy of committee consideration, both for the protection of the petitioner as well as to give credibility to the decisions that this Elouse makes.
It has already been stated that this involves a duly registered company which failed to file the required summaries and was dissolved. That dissolution is listed in The Canada Gazette.
I recognize that many small companies perhaps do not even have the resources to be monitoring such things, but when such a company comes before the House of Commons for discussion I think it is a more serious matter. Given that the company did not recognize that it was dissolved and continued to operate for close to another 20 years, one assumes that it did not submit the required summaries during that time, as it had not done before dissolution. Therefore, while not suggesting that there was a deliberate intent to mislead, certainly the company displayed poor management practices. Furthermore, while we are not discussing the assets which the company washes to recover, we are not aware of their dollar value.
Given that there have been some rather unorthodox practices by this company which continued to operate for 20 years in which it presumably did not even submit the required summaries, we are supporting the motion that the Bill go to committee.
However, being from the north myself, 1 realize that these companies often work with very small resources and may overlook such things. Therefore, I hope the committee could expedite this as quickly as possible so that the matter can be redressed in the best manner possible.

speechtext:
Madam Speaker, I can assure you that I will be brief. The reason I am speaking is that the company is located in the area that I represent.
Today we are dealing with a very simple administrative, pro forma type of matter. It is almost unbelievable that the NDP would be so obstructionist as not to allow all three stages of the
Bill to be dealt with this afternoon. There is absolutely no reason why we should debate it, at considerable expense to the taxpayers of Canada and to the company officials involved. However, if that is the way they like to operate, I guess we must live with them.
What I do want to do, Madam Speaker, is to pay tribute to the Yellowknife Electric Company, which has not operated now for several years but at one time was a force to be reckoned with in the electrical contracting field, and to pay tribute to the principles of that company, in particular Mr. A1 Marceau, who has done much for the City of Yellowknife over many years. I promised to be brief, Madam Speaker, and I was brief.
